It was performed by 18 teams, and [[R.S.C. Anderlecht]] won the championship, while [[K. Waterschei S.V. Thor Genk]] & [[Lierse S.K. (1906)|Lierse S.K.]] were relegated.<ref name="rsssf">{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesb/belghist.html |title=Belgium – Final Tables 1895–2008 |publisher=The Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation |last1=Ploquin |first1=Phil |last2=Nackaerts |first2=Luc |last3=Coolsaet |first3=Jeroen |access-date=17 December 2018}}</ref>

The top two teams, Anderlecht and [[Club Brugge K.V.|Club Brugge]], finished level on points (though Anderlecht had a superior [[goal difference]]) and it was decided that a two-legged championship playoff would take place – a situation which had not occurred in Belgian football since [[1928–29 Belgian First Division|1928–29]]. Both of these 'test matches' were drawn: 1–1 in [[Brussels]] and 2–2 in [[Bruges]], with Anderlecht coming back from two goals behind and holding off a late onslaught from the opposition to claim the title on the [[away goals rule]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nieuwsblad.be/cnt/2d2ah081 |title=Reconstructie van de memorabele testmatchen van 1986 |trans-title=Reconstruction of the memorable test matches of 1986 |newspaper=Nieuwsblad|author=Marc Reunes|language=nl|date=19 May 2009|access-date=12 April 2024}}</ref>
